newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee hits 15-1/2 mth peak in fund-led rally.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee hits 15-1/2 mth peak in fund-led rally.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures shot up to 15-1/2 month high in a new rally on Friday fired by a wave of fund and technical-related buying. Trading was brisk.
Benchmark July clinched more than a six percent gain on the day as speculative and hedge funds swarmed the market from the opening bell.

"The market is clearing every strong resistance levels on the way up and this attracted new fund interest," said one trader. Volatility has also improved as the market moved out of its dull and familiar trading ranges that marked the late April trading.
July charged to a high of $2,060 a tonne, the highest since January 31, 1996, after vaulting above the closely-watched $2,000 barrier. It fell back to end midsession a hefty $101 up at $2,034.
But long liquidation seeped in during the afternoon as New York arabica futures retraced after a dazzling performance on Thursday, pushing robustas into the minus column.
It met roaster support at the lows and the market soon rebounded towards the finish as fund buying re-emerged. Origin and trade sellers were seen at the highs.
September and November also firmed in brisk trade as buyers moved further out.
Traders said the funds had been massively long in robustas since the frenzied buying from early January that triggered the current five-month rally.
"The funds are about 8,000 to 10,000-lot longs in robustas," said one European coffee trader.
Traders noted light origin offers this morning but added producers could return on a large scale if the market continued to climb.
The arabicas soared to 20-year highs basis May on Thursday in a dizzy rally on frantic buying from speculators and commercial coffee firms worried about low reserves and poor crop prospects.
Jitters over the fast approaching Brazilian frost season could help sustain the current rally.
This week's surge in bean prices could trigger fresh retail price hikes by roasters in Europe after having to put up prices in March and April.

Roasters warned that if prices stay at these levels, coffee consumption could fall by up to 10 million bags a year on a global basis as consumers turn to other alternatives such as tea and soft drinks.
Market attention will focus on key producer talks in London on Monday and Wednesday to consider the future of their current export quota programme beyond June this year.

The U.S. green coffee stock data for April released on Thursday were seen as neutral. The stocks showed a rise of 198,000 bags against market expectations of 100,000 to 300,000 bags. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
